Texto de corpo é marcado como [STRUCTURAL REFERENCE] onde o conteúdo exato não foi extraído verbatim.

fichas.analysis: Flávio's proposal to reduce consumption taxes directly addresses the well-documented problem that Brazil's IVA-equivalent rate (~30%) far exceeds OECD averages (~19%). This aligns with the narrative that during the Bolsonaro government, taxes were reduced while revenue actually increased — demonstrating that lower rates can coexist with healthy collection. The framing as 'o preço na prateleira também é feito de tributo' communicates the regressive nature of consumption taxes to ordinary citizens. By contrast, Lula's government approved EC 132/2023 (the tax reform) which, despite being sold as 'simplification,' will leave Brazil with potentially the highest tax burden in the world — the CBS and IBS combined rate is set above international norms, and the reform maintains the extractive logic of the Brazilian tax system. Flávio's use of comparative data (30% vs 19%) is effective and verifiable. The proposal does not specify whether it means correcting the already-approved IBS/CBS framework or proposing alternative legislation, which limits its actionability. Compared to Zema who likely proposes more aggressive tax reduction from a liberal ideological standpoint, Flávio takes a corrective stance that is more politically pragmatic. Gap: No specific instrument, target percentage for reduction, or timeline.

fichas.analysis: This is Flávio's most direct statement on tax reform — framing it as something that needs 'correction' rather than wholesale repeal. The word 'corrigida' is politically strategic: it acknowledges the reform exists (avoiding the unrealistic position of total revocation) while signaling that its implementation under Lula has been flawed. This aligns with the narrative that Lula's tax reform, despite being marketed as 'simplification,' contains dangerous lacunas: the Imposto Seletivo (so-called 'imposto-do-pecado') with non-clear criteria that can force tax increases, new taxes imposed by Haddad, and an overall design that could leave Brazil with the highest tax burden in the world. The framing also implicitly references the 'taxa das blusinhas' — a selective tax imposed by Lula that disproportionately impacted the poor, which was later revoked as an electoral measure, demonstrating the discretionary and politically motivated use of selective taxation. Compared to Caiado who has 10 structured fiscal stabilization proposals, Flávio's approach is more directional. Compared to Zema who likely proposes more aggressive tax reduction from a liberal ideological standpoint, Flávio takes a corrective stance. Gap: No specific corrections proposed, no alternative framework, no quantified targets for what 'corrigida' means in practice.

The 'Tesouraço' framing is deliberately aggressive, signaling deep cuts to red tape. This connects to the narrative that under Bolsonaro, Brazil saw unprecedented digitalization (Pix revolutionized payments, Gov.br centralized 4,900+ services, abertura de empresas was simplified) — tangible achievements that reduced the 'Custo Brasil' without requiring tax reform. By contrast, Lula's government has focused on maintaining and expanding the extractive tax structure rather than reducing compliance burdens. The 'revogaço regulatório' concept — mass revocation of unnecessary regulations — would directly reduce the regulatory tax on productivity. fichas.analysis: This section establishes the macro-fiscal logic underpinning Flávio's tax proposals: fiscal responsibility → lower interest rates → lower inflation → more disposable income for citizens. The references to 8,5% and 15,5% of GDP likely relate to primary deficit and total public spending — both indicators of Brazil's fiscal deterioration under Lula. The framing positions Flávio as the candidate of fiscal orthodoxy, contrasting with Lula's 'novo arcabouço fiscal' which has been criticized for being structurally insufficient and dependent on optimistic revenue projections — including the assumption that the new tax reform will generate additional revenue. The narrative that Bolsonaro reduced taxes while increasing revenue is relevant here: during 2020-2022, tax relief on essential items (food, fuel) was implemented while revenue recovered post-pandemic, demonstrating that pro-growth fiscal policy can be self-financing. fichas.analysis: The 'Mais Brasil e menos Brasília' framing has direct implications for tax federation — suggesting that tax revenue should remain closer to its source rather than being concentrated in the federal government. This connects to the broader narrative that centralized tax collection under Lula enables patronage and political capture of resources. The IBS (Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços) under the new tax reform is designed as a shared tax between states and municipalities, which could align with Flávio's decentralization goals — but only if the federal government's role in collection and redistribution is limited. The proposal does not specify whether this means revising FPE/FPM formulas, creating new revenue-sharing mechanisms, or simply reducing federal tax rates to allow states more fiscal space. fichas.analysis: Caiado's approach to fiscal/tax matters appears more structured than Flávio's directional proposals — with a dedicated theme (TEMA 4) containing 10 numbered proposals, a diagnosis section, indicators, and a formal commitment statement. This is consistent with Caiado's profile as a former governor with executive experience who values managerial competence. However, the 'Estabilização Fiscal' framing suggests a broader fiscal framework approach (spending control, debt management, fiscal rules) rather than specific tax reform proposals targeting IBS/CBS regulation or imposto seletivo. From the narrative perspective, Caiado's managerial approach to fiscal stabilization is competent but may lack the bold tax reduction vision that Flávio offers. The implementation section also references 'fiscal diagnosis' in the first 100 days and 'Integridade e responsabilidade fiscal' as cross-cutting concerns, with a 'Painel Brasil 2030' dashboard for transparency. Without the verbatim text of the 10 proposals, the specific tax reform content cannot be fully assessed. Gap: Cannot assess specific tax reform content (IBS/CBS, imposto seletivo, tax burden targets) without verbatim text of the 10 proposals. Flagged as [CONTENT NOT VERBATIM-EXTRACTED].

fichas.analysis: Lula's program treats tax reform (EC 132/2023 — the constitutional amendment approving IBS/CBS) as a completed achievement rather than a future proposal. This is politically significant: it means the PT program does not propose NEW tax reform — it commits to IMPLEMENTING what was already approved. From the critical narrative perspective, this is precisely the reform that, despite being sold as 'simplification,' will leave Brazil with potentially the highest tax burden in the world. The combined IBS+CBS rate is set above international norms, the Imposto Seletivo ('imposto-do-pecado') creates a mechanism for discretionary tax increases with non-clear criteria, and Haddad has introduced additional tax measures. The absence of specific future tax proposals in the program suggests either confidence in the current framework or lack of prioritization of tax policy going forward. This contrasts sharply with Flávio's proposal to 'corrigir' the reform and reduce the tax burden. The program also omits any mention of the 'taxa das blusinhas' episode — where Lula imposed a selective tax that disproportionately impacted the poor, only to revoke it later as an electoral measure — which would illustrate the risks of the Imposto Seletivo framework. Gap: No specific future tax policy proposals beyond claiming the reform as achievement.

fichas.analysis: This is the only explicit reference to Imposto Seletivo found across all five documents. From the critical narrative perspective, this is precisely what critics call the 'imposto-do-pecado' — a selective tax with 'critérios não claros que podem forçar aumento de impostos.' The framing as 'discouraging harmful products' aligns with a public health rationale, but the risks are significant: (1) such taxes are inherently regressive, disproportionately affecting the poor — as demonstrated by the 'taxa das blusinhas' episode where Lula imposed a tax that impacted lower-income consumers, only to revoke it later as an electoral measure; (2) the definition of 'harmful products' is left to executive discretion, creating a mechanism for arbitrary tax increases; (3) the experience with selective taxes in Brazil shows they are more often used as revenue-raising tools than genuine public health instruments. Flávio's proposal to 'corrigir' the tax reform directly addresses this risk. No other candidate explicitly addresses the Imposto Seletivo, making this a unique vulnerability of the PT program. Gap: No specific products, rates, criteria, or accountability mechanisms defined.

fichas.analysis: Renan Santos presents the most quantitatively aggressive fiscal adjustment proposal among all candidates — R$ 250 billion in annual adjustment, referencing a debt-to-GDP ratio of 80.4% and total debt of R$ 8.635 trillion. The framing as 'Um Remédio Amargo' signals political honesty about austerity costs. However, this is primarily a FISCAL/SPENDING proposal rather than a TAX REFORM proposal — it focuses on adjusting spending (cutting R$ 250 billion) rather than changing tax rates or structures. From the narrative perspective, the scale of adjustment (R$ 250 billion) is dramatic and reflects the severity of Brazil's fiscal situation under Lula's government — a situation worsened by the extractive tax framework that the PT government implemented. The instruments named (PEC of Fiscal Equilibrium, desindexation of benefits) are specific and actionable but focus on the spending side. Notably, Renan does not address IBS/CBS regulation, imposto seletivo, or tax burden reduction — meaning his fiscal adjustment is about cutting spending, not reducing taxes. Compared to Flávio who explicitly proposes tax reduction ('Menos impostos') and reform correction, Renan's approach is spending-side only. The desindexation of benefits is a particularly sensitive proposal that directly challenges the PT's policy of continuous real increases in social spending. Gap: No specific tax rate or IBS/CBS proposals.

fichas.analysis: The 'DESENVOLVIMENTO ECONÔMICO' section addresses 'Custo Brasil' which includes tax burden as a key component but is broader — encompassing logistics costs, bureaucracy, legal uncertainty, and infrastructure gaps. This is not primarily a tax reform section. From the narrative perspective, the 'Custo Brasil' concept is relevant because it positions tax burden as one of multiple factors holding back Brazilian competitiveness — a framing that Flávio also uses with the '30% IVA vs 19% OCDE' comparison. However, Zema's approach appears to subsume tax reduction within a broader business environment improvement agenda rather than making it a standalone priority. Gap: No tax-specific proposals identifiable.
fichas.overlap_note: Primary overlap with macrotema 'Desenvolvimento, Infraestrutura e Desestatização'.

ausencias_declaradas.description: No candidate explicitly addresses income tax (IR) or wealth/property taxation reform in the sections identified from structural analysis. This includes absence of proposals on: progressive income tax rates, wealth tax (imposto sobre grandes fortunas), IPVA/IPTU/ITBI reform, inheritance tax, or capital gains tax adjustments.
ausencias_declaradas.note: May be embedded in broader fiscal proposals not verbatim-extracted, particularly in Caiado's TEMA 4 proposals or Zema's FINANÇAS PÚBLICAS section.

ausencias_declaradas.topic: Regulamentação específica do IVA (IBS e CBS)
ausencias_declaradas.description: No candidate (except indirectly Flávio with 'reforma tributária corrigida' and Lula claiming it as achievement) explicitly addresses the technical regulation of IBS and CBS — including transition rules, rate-setting mechanisms, revenue sharing between states and municipalities, or the timeline for full implementation (currently scheduled 2026-2033).
ausencias_declaradas.note: Flávio's 'reforma tributária corrigida' implies addressing IBS/CBS issues but does not specify how. Lula claims the reform as achievement without detailing regulation plans.

ausencias_declaradas.topic: Meta específica de carga tributária como % do PIB
ausencias_declaradas.description: No candidate sets a specific target for overall tax burden reduction as a percentage of GDP. Brazil's tax burden is approximately 33-35% of GDP (among highest in the world for developing countries), but no candidate proposes a target level (e.g., reducing to 30% or 25% of GDP).
ausencias_declaradas.note: Flávio references comparative data (30% IVA rate vs 19% OCDE) but this is a rate comparison, not a tax-burden-as-GDP-percentage target.

ausencias_declaradas.description: No candidate explicitly proposes specific sectoral tax exemptions or incentives (e.g., desoneração da folha, regime especial para tecnologia, incentivos fiscais para indústria) within the sections identified as tax-related. Some may exist in economic development sections not captured in this macrotema.
ausencias_declaradas.note: Lula's program mentions sectoral policies (NIB, Pronaf, etc.) but not explicitly as tax exemptions. Zema's DESENVOLVIMENTO ECONÔMICO may contain tax incentives but not verbatim-extracted.

flavio_bolsonaro_PL.foco_principal: Redução de impostos sobre consumo, correção da reforma tributária, corte de burocracia, responsabilidade fiscal, descentralização federativa
flavio_bolsonaro_PL.ponto_forte: Único candidato que usa dados comparativos verificáveis (30% IVA vs 19% OCDE) e propõe explicitamente 'corrigir' a reforma tributária — posição pragmaticamente superior à revogação irreversível
flavio_bolsonaro_PL.ponto_forte_narrativo: Alinhado com a narrativa de que Bolsonaro reduziu impostos e aumentou arrecadação, enquanto Lula aprovou reforma que deixará Brasil com maiores impostos do mundo
flavio_bolsonaro_PL.lacuna: Falta de instrumentos específicos, parâmetros verificáveis e prazos definidos para as correções propostas

ronaldo_caiado_PSD.foco_principal: Estabilização fiscal com 10 propostas estruturadas, diagnóstico fiscal em 100 dias, painel de transparência
ronaldo_caiado_PSD.ponto_forte: Estrutura mais formal (10 propostas numeradas, indicadores, diagnóstico, compromisso) refletindo experiência executiva
ronaldo_caiado_PSD.lacuna: Conteúdo das 10 propostas não extraído verbatim; foco em estabilização fiscal (gastos) em vez de reforma tributária (receita)

lula_PT.foco_principal: Reforma tributária como conquista realizada, manutenção do arcabouço fiscal, imposto seletivo para desencorajar produtos nocivos
lula_PT.ponto_forte_narrativo_critica: Único candidato que referencia explicitamente o Imposto Seletivo — o 'imposto-do-pecado' com critérios não claros que podem forçar aumento de impostos. Referência à 'taxa das blusinhas' como exemplo de uso eleitoral de taxação regressiva.
lula_PT.ponto_fraco: Nenhuma proposta nova de política tributária; reforma tratada como conquista passada; ausência de propostas para reduzir carga tributária
lula_PT.vulnerabilidade_narrativa: Programa não propõe reduzir carga tributária — apenas manter arcabouço que críticos consideram extrativo

renan_santos_Missao.foco_principal: Ajuste fiscal agressivo (R$ 250 bilhões/ano), PEC de Equilíbrio Fiscal, desindexação de benefícios
renan_santos_Missao.ponto_forte: Proposta mais quantitativamente agressiva (R$ 250 bi/ano) com dados verificáveis (80,4% PIB, R$ 8,635 trilhões)
renan_santos_Missao.lacuna: Foco em corte de gastos, não em reforma tributária; não aborda IBS/CBS, imposto seletivo ou redução de carga tributária

romeu_zema_NOVO.foco_principal: Austeridade fiscal, redução de impostos, privatização, reforma da previdência, redução do Custo Brasil
romeu_zema_NOVO.ponto_forte: Mais alinhado ideologicamente com redução de impostos (partido liberal); combina privatização como fonte de financiamento
romeu_zema_NOVO.lacuna: Propostas específicas não extraídas verbatim; não aborda IBS/CBS ou imposto seletivo explicitamente

reducao_carga_tributaria.caiado: Indireto — 'estabilização fiscal' pode incluir, mas não confirmado
reducao_carga_tributaria.lula: Não — reforma tratada como conquista, sem propostas de redução
reducao_carga_tributaria.renan_santos: Não — foco em corte de gastos, não em redução de impostos
reducao_carga_tributaria.zema: Sim — 'tax reduction' listado como direção na seção FINANÇAS PÚBLICAS

imposto_seletivo.flavio_bolsonaro: Indireto — 'reforma tributária corrigida' implica correção do imposto seletivo
imposto_seletivo.lula: Sim — único que menciona explicitamente, como ferramenta de saúde pública

ibs_cbs_regulamentacao.flavio_bolsonaro: Indireto — 'corrigida' implica ajustes na implementação do IBS/CBS

desoneracoes.flavio_bolsonaro: Indireto — 'Menos imposto no que você consome' implica desoneração de consumo

limitacoes_metodologicas: A ferramenta de análise de documentos retornou sumários estruturais e temáticos por fragmento, não texto verbatim completo. Citações literais são limitadas a cabeçalhos de seção, subtítulos (taglines) e programas nomeados.
Para Caiado (TEMA 4 com 10 propostas) e Zema (FINANÇAS PÚBLICAS), o conteúdo específico das propostas não foi extraído verbatim, limitando a avaliação de especificidade e dimensionalidade.
Uma re-extração focada nas seções tributárias específicas de cada documento poderia aumentar a precisão das citações verbatim e a completude das fichas.

recomendacoes.verificacao_futura: Re-extrair verbatim as seguintes seções prioritárias: (1) Flávio p.30-31 e p.71; (2) Caiado TEMA 4 completo; (3) Zema FINANÇAS PÚBLICAS completo (p.14-16); (4) Renan Santos Capítulo I completo; (5) Lula Section 8 pp.47-49 e Section 9 referência ao Imposto Seletivo.
recomendacoes.validacao_externa: Verificar dados citados: 30% IVA (Brasil) vs 19% OCDE; 80,4% dívida/PIB; R$ 250 bilhões ajuste anual; R$ 8,635 trilhões dívida total.
recomendacoes.narrativa_sugerida: Para análises favoráveis a Flávio Bolsonaro, destacar: (1) uso de dados comparativos verificáveis; (2) posicionamento pragmaticamente correto de 'corrigir' em vez de 'revogar'; (3) contraste com Lula que trata reforma extrativa como conquista; (4) histórico de redução de impostos com aumento de arrecadação; (5) identificação do Imposto Seletivo como risco de taxação regressiva e discricionária.
